Unfortunately for them, however, nightmares like this can sometimes become reality. After Iran effectively shut down the straight of Hormuz during its war with America and Israel, the Saudis were largely able to continue on more or less unscathed for a while by diverting the majority of their oil exports over to their western Red Sea coast instead via their East West crude oil pipeline. Originally built in the early 1980s to hedge against Saudi Arabia's then overwhelming dependency on oil exports through the straight of Hormuz, the East West Pipeline sprawls for more than 12,200 km through the desert and connects the kingdom's oil producing heartland around the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
